html:
The culture of the Iron Age Celts of central and western Europe, from about 450 BCE to the Roman conquest. It is named after a site on Lake Neuchâtel in Switzerland where thousands of objects were found from 1857. The map puts it in 700 BCE in northern France, earlier than its usual start; in 700 BCE the region belonged to the Hallstatt culture that came before.

La Tène art is famous for swirling curves, plant tendrils and strange faces on metalwork, drawing on Greek and Etruscan imports. In Champagne and the Rhineland warriors were buried with two-wheeled chariots.

In the 4th century BCE La Tène peoples spread widely. Gauls routed Rome at the Allia and sacked the city, others such as the Boii settled in Italy, and some attacked Delphi in 279 BCE. Later they built fortified towns called oppida and struck coins. Julius Caesar's Gallic Wars ended their independence in Gaul. The wider story is under Celtic Europe.
